column1: # NFTBan — UNRESOLVED unbounded ownership/mode mutation sites (v1.228.10)
# Consumed by BOTH existing guards — tools/check-recursive-permissions.sh (pre-commit) and
# check_recursive_permissions() in .github/ci/health_check.sh (CI). There is no third guard.
# THIS IS NOT AN ALLOWLIST. A row means STILL WRONG, deliberately deferred, with a named
# owner decision. Rows are printed on every run so the debt stays visible, the count may
# only DECREASE, and a site that is NOT listed fails the build immediately.
# All six rows are one open item: OPEN_DEBT — GO FALLBACK PARITY (owner TODO-3).
# internal/installer/fhs/permissions.go::applyPermissions is the installer's FALLBACK
# permission path, reached only when the generated primary script is missing or fails
# (fhs/permissions.go SetPermissions). It maintains its own recursive ownership logic
# instead of deriving from the canonical matrix in build/fhs-spec.yaml, so it is WEAKER
# than the primary path it stands in for.
#   INVARIANT: RECOVERY/FALLBACK MUST NOT BE WEAKER THAN PRIMARY.
# The canonical-permission lane may not close until these either converge to the canonical
# matrix or are separated into an approved follow-up with a hard release gate (owner ruling
# 2026-08-09). The primary path for LogDir is already fixed at the spec level (226e49b5);
# :89 remains here precisely because fixing the spec did NOT fix the fallback.
# columns: file:line<TAB>reason
internal/installer/fhs/permissions.go:78
column2: GO_FALLBACK_PARITY — EtcDir /etc/nftban root:nftban. Highest-priority sibling: recursive over OPERATOR-CREATED config (whitelist.d/, blacklist.d/). Owner-required read-only classification before any change.

column1: internal/installer/fhs/permissions.go:82
column2: GO_FALLBACK_PARITY — BinDir /usr/lib/nftban/bin root:root. Package-owned binaries; foreign content unlikely but UNMEASURED.

column1: internal/installer/fhs/permissions.go:85
column2: GO_FALLBACK_PARITY — DataDir /var/lib/nftban. Would flatten the root:nftban admin roots (backup/, update-backups/, pro/) and the root:nftban-auditor 0770 evidence boundary that the primary path preserves.

column1: internal/installer/fhs/permissions.go:89
column2: GO_FALLBACK_PARITY — LogDir /var/log/nftban. The primary path was fixed at the canonical spec (226e49b5); this fallback still claims every descendant, so the invariant is not yet closed end-to-end.

column1: internal/installer/fhs/permissions.go:93
column2: GO_FALLBACK_PARITY — CacheDir /var/cache/nftban 0755 world-traversable; foreign-content reachability unmeasured.

column1: internal/installer/fhs/permissions.go:97
column2: GO_FALLBACK_PARITY — RunDir /run/nftban. tmpfs, recreated per boot, so foreign persistence is bounded by definition. Lowest risk of the six; still requires the explicit classification.
